items.title: Dogwood Festival, 2nd Weekend in April
items.content_text: Held Friday through Sunday in Atlanta, Georgia, the Dogwood Festival is the city’s oldest fine arts festival. Dogwood trees are in full bloom, and artists from around the country display their work. All art is welcome, from paintings to photographs and sculptures to jewelry. There’s also music and food to round out the celebrations. Created in 1936 to boost community spirit during the Great Depression and celebrate Atlanta’s native dogwood trees. items.title: Neurodiversity Pride Day, June 16
items.content_text: Neurodiversity Pride Day was created in 2018 by the Neurodiversity Foundation to recognize and embrace neurological differences. It’s a day organized by neurodivergent people, for neurodivergent people, and their allies. This is part of a broader Neurodiversity Pride Week, with events leading up to this day. “Neurodiversity” refers to the idea that differences in how people’s brains work are natural and valuable, not deficits. items.title: National Chicken Noodle Soup Day, March 13
items.content_text: National Chicken Noodle Soup Day honors one of the most comforting and iconic soups in American cuisine. While numerous chicken soups exist, today’s focus is on those featuring noodles, which is fitting given that it’s also National Noodle Month. Chicken noodle soup brings comfort when it’s cold outside. It’s a traditional remedy when feeling sick. items.title: National Cheese Doodle Day, March 5
items.content_text: National Cheese Doodle Day is all about cheese doodles, those bright-orange corn snacks. These puffy, crispy corn snacks coated in cheese go by many names, including cheese puffs, cheese curls, cheese balls, corn curls, and cheese doodles. They were invented in the United States in the 1930s. There are competing accounts on who invented them, but the most accepted credits Morrie Yohai for Old London Foods. items.title: National Ranch Dressing Day, March 10
items.content_text: National Ranch Dressing Day is a dedicated to America’s most popular salad dressing, a position held since 1992. The day celebrates ranch dressing, the creamy, tangy condiment used as a salad dressing and as a dip. It’s made with buttermilk, garlic, onion, mustard, herbs (commonly chives, parsley, and dill), and spices. items.title: National Moscow Mule Day, March 3
items.content_text: National Moscow Mule Day was created in 2016–2017 by SMIRNOFF™ Vodka along with Foodimentary.com to acknowledge the cocktail’s legacy and its place in drink culture. They chose the date (3-3) to represent the cocktail’s three core ingredients: vodka, ginger beer, and lime. If you rotate 3-3 counterclockwise, the numbers become M-M for Moscow Mule. items.content_text: not the official logo Rare Disease Day was created in 2008 by the European Organisation for Rare Diseases to raise awareness for unknown or overlooked illnesses and improve access to treatment and medical representation for individuals with rare diseases and their families. It’s celebrated on the last day of February, the 28th or 29th in leap years. They're over 7,000 rare diseases, and about 300 million people worldwide live with one. items.title: Pluto Day, February 18
items.content_text: Photo Credit: NASA/JHUAPL/SwRI Pluto Day commemorates the discovered a tiny, distant planet on February 18, 1930 by astronomer Clyde W. Tombaugh. After other astronomers confirmed his finding, they publicly announced the discovery of Pluto on March 13, 1930. Back then, people hailed Pluto as the ninth planet. items.content_text: Wine Day, also known as Red Day in South Korea, is an unofficial romantic holiday celebrated on October 14th. Couples celebrate with wine, usually red wine.
